title: A Setting, Not a Sacrifice
story: When the new intercom stayed open after every delivery, Farah heard the stairwell all evening. She asked the installer to shorten the release rather than mute her handset, because muting would also hide a genuine call. He cut the open interval and tested it with her. Parcels arrived. The flat stayed quiet unless someone meant to speak. A setting, not a sacrifice, had settled the dispute.

vocabulary.definition: A device for speaking to someone at the door
The part that kept the line open after a buzz
The part of the phone she held or answered
The length of time something stays open

quiz.question: What change did Farah request from the installer?
options: A shorter time with the line left open
A handset that stayed silent all evening
An end to parcel deliveries
A louder stairwell for every call
quiz.correctAnswer: A shorter time with the line left open
quiz.explanation: She asked him to shorten the release instead of muting the handset.
quiz.supportingSentence: She asked the installer to shorten the release rather than mute her handset, because muting would also hide a genuine call.

quiz.question: What continued after the open interval was cut?
options: Parcels still came
The stairwell noise lasted all evening
Genuine calls were hidden
The installer removed the handset
quiz.explanation: The story says parcels arrived after he tested the shorter interval.

quiz.question: Why was muting the handset a poor fix?
options: It would have hidden a real call as well as the noise
The installer could visit only after midnight
Parcels had to be carried up a silent stair
The building had banned genuine callers
quiz.correctAnswer: It would have hidden a real call as well as the noise
quiz.explanation: Muting would have stopped the noise and also stopped a call she still needed to hear.
quiz.supportingSentence: She asked the installer to shorten the release rather than mute her handset, because muting would also hide a genuine call.

quiz.question: What does interval mean in this passage?
options: The stretch of time the line stayed open
A parcel left beside the door
A person who installs locks
A dispute between neighbours
quiz.correctAnswer: The stretch of time the line stayed open
quiz.explanation: He cut the open interval, meaning he reduced how long the intercom stayed live.
quiz.supportingSentence: He cut the open interval and tested it with her.

quiz.question: Why does the writer contrast a setting with a sacrifice?
options: To show the fix was an adjustment rather than a loss
To prove parcels should stop after dusk
To suggest the installer muted the whole building
To argue that stairwells ought to stay noisy
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the fix was an adjustment rather than a loss
quiz.explanation: The closing line says a setting, rather than a sacrifice, settled the dispute.
quiz.supportingSentence: A setting, not a sacrifice, had settled the dispute.
